chapter: Violin, clarinet and the family name
title: Joining Basie in 1951 as clarinetist replacing Buddy De Franco
summary: Royal joined Basie in January 1951 mainly as a clarinet player, in a small group with Clark Terry and Wardell Gray.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: No, nobody writes for a clarinet. So if you don't write for it, you don't play it. But that was pretty well my favorite instrument. As a matter of fact, when I went to work with the Basie Band in '51, when I went -- that was January, 1951 -- I went to his band primarily as a clarinet player, because I was replacing Buddy De Franco, who was an excellent clarinet player, one of the best jazz clarinet players there ever was. So, in replacing him, Basie was kind enough to remember that I was an exceptional player. So I went in there and I had to be an exceptional player because the company

of the other two horns was extremely perilous. Clark Terry was playing the trumpet and Wardell Grey (PHONETIC) was playing the tenor saxophone and if you couldn't play, you just as well go home with them.

So, it was very interesting, because we only had the three horns and it was a workout every night and if you couldn't play clarinet in that band -- if you couldn't play clarinet, period -- you just couldn't hold that job. So, it was a lot of fun.
